goal: Implement score(rolls) in bowling.py returning the total score of a complete ten-pin bowling game.
behaviors: score([0] * 20) returns 0 (open frames with no pins, summing rolls frame by frame).
score([3, 4] * 10) returns 70 (open frames with nonzero rolls sum to their pin counts).
score([5, 5, 3] + [0] * 17) returns 16 (a spare scores 10 plus the next roll, so frame 1 is 13 and frame 2 is 3).
score([10, 3, 4] + [0] * 16) returns 24 (a strike scores 10 plus the next two rolls, so frame 1 is 17 and frame 2 is 7).
score([0] * 18 + [5, 5, 7]) returns 17 (a spare in the tenth frame earns one bonus roll, counted once).
score([10] * 12) returns 300 and score([0] * 18 + [10, 10, 10]) returns 30 (a strike in the tenth frame earns two bonus rolls, and a perfect game scores 300).

assumptions.text: bowling.py exists in the repo root as the one flat module.
The tests/ folder exists for the new test file.
pyproject.toml exists so the toolchain configuration is present.
Python 3.10 or newer is available for the implementation.
pytest can be imported to run the tests.

demo: python -c 'from bowling import score; print(score([0] * 20)); print(score([10] * 12))'
out_of_scope: Validating input: rolls are always a valid, complete game.
Per-frame score breakdowns or running totals.
A command-line interface or any I/O.
Support for games other than ten-pin bowling.
